questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What is a principal advantage of offline retrieval evaluation?
options: It is repeatable and does not expose users to experimental rankings
It measures every aspect of user value directly
It cannot contain judgment bias
It removes the need for online monitoring

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What does random assignment in an online A/B test primarily support?
options: Complete relevance judgments
Causal comparison between eligible treatment and control traffic
Identical user behavior in both variants
Removal of all logging errors

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: Why can click-through rate misrepresent relevance?
options: Clicks are available only offline
Every click means the task failed
Position and presentation can attract clicks independent of usefulness
Relevant results can never be clicked

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What should be checked before interpreting an online metric lift?
options: Only the treatment's average query length
Whether offline nDCG is exactly one
Whether every user clicked something
Assignment integrity, exposure, logging, and sample ratios

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: Offline nDCG rises after long manuals are promoted, but task completion falls. What is a likely diagnosis?
options: The offline relevance model does not fully represent concise task resolution
Online randomization always reverses true effects
nDCG cannot evaluate ranked results
The index contains no manuals

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What is the best response when offline and online results disagree?
options: Always trust clicks and discard labels
Investigate labels, latency, presentation, logging, and metric mechanisms
Ship whichever system has the newer model
Average unrelated metrics into one number

questions.question: Why is a system comparison across the same queries paired?
options: Both systems must return the same documents
Every query has the same metric value
Each query supplies a matched outcome from both systems
The systems must use the same source code

questions.question: What does a confidence interval around the mean paired delta communicate?
options: The probability every relevance label is correct
The number of configurations tested
The business value of the feature
Uncertainty in the estimated average change under the sampling method

questions.question: System A scores [0.4,0.7] and B scores [0.5,0.6]. What are the paired B minus A deltas?
Why should practical significance be assessed in addition to a p-value?
options: A p-value directly measures revenue
A statistically clear effect can still be too small to matter
Practical significance eliminates uncertainty
Only insignificant changes can be useful

questions.question: Why can testing 100 configurations and reporting only the smallest p-value be misleading?
options: Paired differences become impossible
The query set becomes binary
Multiple comparisons increase the chance of a false discovery
Every configuration must have equal scores

questions.question: Many evaluation queries are near-duplicates from the same sessions. Which resampling choice is most defensible?
options: Treat every duplicate as fully independent
Drop the treatment scores
Resample individual metric digits
Resample at a session or appropriate cluster level

questions.question: What is the main purpose of query-class error analysis?
options: Find repeated, actionable mechanisms behind improvements and regressions
Replace all aggregate metrics with anecdotes
Guarantee every class improves equally
Remove queries on which treatment loses

questions.question: Which pair describes two different useful kinds of class label?
options: Document byte size and random number
Query intent and failure mechanism
Control rank and treatment color
Metric mean and confidence level

questions.question: What evidence should accompany a mean metric delta for a query class?
options: Only one winning example
The system's repository size
Class count, baseline, uncertainty, win rate, and severe regressions
The total number of vocabulary terms only

questions.question: Why should newly discovered post-hoc classes be treated as hypotheses?
options: Class labels cannot describe production queries
Post-hoc classes always contain label errors
Only online experiments permit slices
Repeated slicing can manufacture apparently strong patterns by chance

questions.question: A relevant document is absent from the final top k. What is the best first diagnostic sequence?
options: Trace corpus presence, indexing, candidate sources, fusion, reranking, and filters
Increase every score without inspection
Assume the relevance label is wrong
Change the metric cutoff until it appears

questions.question: A hybrid ranker improves broad queries but harms exact error codes because semantic candidates crowd out lexical matches. What is a targeted remedy?
options: Remove all exact-match indexing
Protect exact-match candidates or use query-dependent fusion
Give every semantic candidate grade zero
Evaluate only broad queries
